Founded in 1948 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, Varian was acquired by Siemens Healthineers in April 2021 for $16.4 billion. Varian continues to operate as a brand within Siemens Healthineers, and its oncology software products are now marketed under both the Varian and Siemens Healthineers Cancer Care brands (the varian.com domain redirects to cancercare.siemens-healthineers.com for software product pages).\n     9→\n    10→Varian's primary software product is the ARIA Oncology Information System, an oncology-specific EMR/EHR that manages radiation, medical, and surgical oncology information. ARIA is the leading best-of-breed oncology information system (OIS) in the US market by revenue. According to Enlyft, approximately 369 organizations use ARIA, with 85% in the United States, 65% in the hospital & healthcare sector, and 59% being large organizations with over 1,000 employees. Varian's customers include major academic medical centers and health systems — a 2024 deal with Ballad Health for a 10-year oncology collaboration included ARIA CORE as a key component.\n    11→\n    12→The intended users listed in the ONC certification are: \"Registered nurses, nurse practitioners, therapist, medical doctors\" — reflecting the clinical staff in radiation and medical oncology departments.\n    13→\n    14→## Product: ARIA CORE\n    15→\n    16→CHPL IDs: 11719\n    17→\n    18→### What It Is\n    19→\n    20→ARIA CORE (v18.3, certified 2025-11-26) is the current-generation oncology management system from Varian, replacing the legacy ARIA Oncology Information System. It is described as a modernized platform \"built for and by oncology experts\" that brings together capabilities from the legacy ARIA OIS with new features. ARIA CORE is designed as a comprehensive, oncology-specific electronic health record that combines radiation oncology, medical oncology, and surgical oncology information into a single workspace.\n    21→\n    22→The certified module — ARIA CORE — is a full oncology information system, not a component of a larger general-purpose EHR. For example, Duke University Health System implemented ARIA alongside their enterprise EMR, using ARIA for radiation oncology-specific data and workflows while the enterprise system handled general clinical data. 422→ \n   423→\n   424→\n   425→ \n   426→ \n   427→ FHIR® Mapping \n   428→ \n   429→ This section discusses the various FHIR® Sections mapped to the USCDI using the FHIR® API platform. \n   430→ \n   431→ \n   432→ Varian SMART on FHIR® API allows other health IT applications to make read-only data requests for patient health information that is part of the USCDI. \n   433→ §170.315(g)(7), FHIR® Mapping \n \n This section discusses the various FHIR® Sections mapped to the USCDI using the FHIR® API platform. \n \n \n Varian SMART on FHIR® API allows other health IT applications to make read-only data requests for patient health information that is part of the USCDI. \n §170.315(g)(7), §170.315(g)(9) and §170.315(g)(10) - API interface would allow a request for “all” the patient data, or specific “by specific data category.” Available data via the API interface is limited by the data defined by the USCDI. \n Varian FHIR® API assumes the use of a cumulative C-CDA with patient data. For filtering C-CDA data by section, it will use the latest cumulative C-CDA document (by the document EffectiveDateTime) per patient. When handling requests for “all patient data,” it will look across all C-CDAs that have been received. \n \n \n \n \n Varian SMART on FHIR® API server maps FHIR® resources to USCDIs \n \n FHIR&reg; API Base URL: \n https://varian.dynamicfhir.com/fhir/varian/basepractice/r4 \n FHIR&reg; It is not querying the native ARIA database.\n\n### CHPL b(10) metadata\n\nThe CHPL listing reveals that:\n- The EHI export relies on **Winzip** as additional software, suggesting the export is a compressed file archive\n- The conformance method is **Attestation** (the vendor attested to compliance rather than having it tested by a testing lab)\n- The export documentation URL is non-functional\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\n**This is a significant finding: there is no publicly accessible documentation of the (b)(10) EHI export.** The only documentation available is the FHIR API portal, which is explicitly a (g)(10) USCDI-scoped API, not a (b)(10) export of all electronic health information.\n\nBased on the product research, ARIA CORE stores extensive oncology-specific data that would be in a patient's designated record set:\n\n| Data Domain | Covered by FHIR API? | Notes |\n|-------------|----------------------|-------|\n| Patient demographics | Yes | Patient resource |\n| Problem lists / diagnoses | Yes | Condition resource |\n| Allergies | Yes | AllergyIntolerance |\n| Medications (chemotherapy regimens) | Partial | MedicationRequest/Dispense, but 300+ oncology-specific regimens unlikely fully mapped |\n| Lab results | Yes | DiagnosticReport, Observation |\n| Vital signs | Yes | Observation |\n| Immunizations | Yes | Immunization |\n| Clinical notes | Partial | DocumentReference (C-CDA), but oncology-specific note types unclear |\n| **Radiation therapy prescriptions** | **Not documented** | Core ARIA data — RT prescriptions are not a standard FHIR US Core resource |\n| **Treatment plans (dose distributions, beam parameters)** | **Not documented** | Physics-level treatment planning data has no FHIR mapping |\n| **Daily treatment records (fraction logs)** | **Not documented** | Per-fraction radiation delivery logs are ARIA-specific |\n| **On-treatment images (MV, kV, CBCT)** | **Not documented** | DICOM images stored in ARIA; not addressable via FHIR API |\n| **Cancer staging (AJCC)** | **Not documented** | ARIA automates staging; no clear FHIR mapping documented |\n| **Toxicity/adverse event records** | **Not documented** | Oncology-specific grading scales |\n| **Disease response data** | **Not documented** | Treatment outcome tracking |\n| **Billing/charge data (RVU tracking)** | **Not documented** | Coverage resource exists but charge capture is not mapped |\n| **QA reports / chart checks** | **Not documented** | Physics QA data |\n| **Patient-reported outcomes (Noona)** | **Not documented** | External integration |\n| **Survivorship care plans** | **Not documented** | External integration (EQUICARE CS) |\n\nThe FHIR API covers roughly the standard USCDI clinical summary — the same data any general-purpose EHR would expose. It does **not** cover the oncology-specific data that is ARIA's primary reason for existence: radiation therapy plans, treatment delivery records, physics QA, imaging, cancer staging, and chemotherapy-specific regimen management.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nNo EHI export format is documented. The FHIR Bulk Data API produces NDJSON bundles of standard FHIR R4 US Core resources. The Winzip dependency listed in CHPL suggests a separate zip-based export mechanism exists but is undocumented.\n\nThe FHIR API documentation reveals that data flows through C-CDA as an intermediary: \"Varian FHIR API assumes the use of a cumulative C-CDA with patient data.\" This means the API is re-projecting C-CDA content into FHIR resources. C-CDA clinical summaries are inherently USCDI-scoped and would not contain radiation therapy physics data, beam parameters, DICOM images, or other specialty oncology data.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n- **For the FHIR (g)(10) API**: The documentation is reasonably thorough for its scope — it includes authorization flows, resource mappings, search parameters, example responses, and bulk export instructions. A developer could implement a FHIR client against this API.\n- **For the (b)(10) EHI export**: There is no documentation at all. The registered URL is dead (404), and no alternative documentation was found.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\nThe FHIR API documentation provides:\n- Resource-level mapping (USCDI category → FHIR resource type)\n- Supported search parameters per resource\n- Example JSON responses\n- Authentication and authorization details\n\nIt does **not** provide:\n- Field-level data dictionaries\n- Value set definitions (relies on US Core defaults)\n- Cardinality or constraint documentation\n- Any mapping of oncology-specific data to export fields\n- Any documentation of what a (b)(10) export contains\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://cancercare.siemens-healthineers.com/aria/ehi\n- Status: dead (404)\n- Required browser: N/A (URL is dead)\n- Navigation complexity: N/A\n- Anti-bot issues: none encountered\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\n1. **Dead registered URL**: The primary registered EHI documentation URL (`https://varian.com/aria/ehi`) redirects to `cancercare.siemens-healthineers.com/aria/ehi` which returns 404. For a radiation oncology system like ARIA — where the majority of clinically significant data (treatment plans, fraction logs, physics data, DICOM images) lives outside the USCDI scope — using the FHIR API as a (b)(10) export would leave the vast majority of the designated record set unexported.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":520,"cache_read_input_tokens":118859,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":520},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"26297f4a-2647-452b-8862-9ff0e0c46345","uuid":"4e7bbde8-1d10-4672-8672-f316b9797bd8"}

| Notes |\n|-------------|----------------------|-------|\n| Patient demographics | Yes | Patient resource |\n| Problem lists / diagnoses | Yes | Condition resource |\n| Allergies | Yes | AllergyIntolerance |\n| Medications (chemotherapy regimens) | Partial | MedicationRequest/Dispense, but 300+ oncology-specific regimens unlikely fully mapped |\n| Lab results | Yes | DiagnosticReport, Observation |\n| Vital signs | Yes | Observation |\n| Immunizations | Yes | Immunization |\n| Clinical notes | Partial | DocumentReference (C-CDA), but oncology-specific note types unclear |\n| **Radiation therapy prescriptions** | **Not documented** | Core ARIA data — RT prescriptions are not a standard FHIR US Core resource |\n| **Treatment plans (dose distributions, beam parameters)** | **Not documented** | Physics-level treatment planning data has no FHIR mapping |\n| **Daily treatment records (fraction logs)** | **Not documented** | Per-fraction radiation delivery logs are ARIA-specific |\n| **On-treatment images (MV, kV, CBCT)** | **Not documented** | DICOM images stored in ARIA; not addressable via FHIR API |\n| **Cancer staging (AJCC)** | **Not documented** | ARIA automates staging; no clear FHIR mapping documented |\n| **Toxicity/adverse event records** | **Not documented** | Oncology-specific grading scales |\n| **Disease response data** | **Not documented** | Treatment outcome tracking |\n| **Billing/charge data (RVU tracking)** | **Not documented** | Coverage resource exists but charge capture is not mapped |\n| **QA reports / chart checks** | **Not documented** | Physics QA data |\n| **Patient-reported outcomes (Noona)** | **Not documented** | External integration |\n| **Survivorship care plans** | **Not documented** | External integration (EQUICARE CS) |\n\nThe FHIR API covers roughly the standard USCDI clinical summary — the same data any general-purpose EHR would expose. It does **not** cover the oncology-specific data that is ARIA's primary reason for existence: radiation therapy plans, treatment delivery records, physics QA, imaging, cancer staging, and chemotherapy-specific regimen management.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nNo EHI export format is documented. The FHIR Bulk Data API produces NDJSON bundles of standard FHIR R4 US Core resources. The Winzip dependency listed in CHPL suggests a separate zip-based export mechanism exists but is undocumented.\n\nThe FHIR API documentation reveals that data flows through C-CDA as an intermediary: \"Varian FHIR API assumes the use of a cumulative C-CDA with patient data.\" This means the API is re-projecting C-CDA content into FHIR resources. C-CDA clinical summaries are inherently USCDI-scoped and would not contain radiation therapy physics data, beam parameters, DICOM images, or other specialty oncology data.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n- **For the FHIR (g)(10) API**: The documentation is reasonably thorough for its scope — it includes authorization flows, resource mappings, search parameters, example responses, and bulk export instructions. A developer could implement a FHIR client against this API.\n- **For the (b)(10) EHI export**: There is no documentation at all. The registered URL is dead (404), and no alternative documentation was found.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\nThe FHIR API documentation provides:\n- Resource-level mapping (USCDI category → FHIR resource type)\n- Supported search parameters per resource\n- Example JSON responses\n- Authentication and authorization details\n\nIt does **not** provide:\n- Field-level data dictionaries\n- Value set definitions (relies on US Core defaults)\n- Cardinality or constraint documentation\n- Any mapping of oncology-specific data to export fields\n- Any documentation of what a (b)(10) export contains\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://cancercare.siemens-healthineers.com/aria/ehi\n- Status: dead (404)\n- Required browser: N/A (URL is dead)\n- Navigation complexity: N/A\n- Anti-bot issues: none encountered\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\n1. **Dead registered URL**: The primary registered EHI documentation URL (`https://varian.com/aria/ehi`) redirects to `cancercare.siemens-healthineers.com/aria/ehi` which returns 404. The combination of a recent certification, attestation-only conformance for (b)(10), and dead documentation URL suggests the EHI export documentation may have been planned but never published.\n\n5. **g(10) conflation**: The only export-related documentation available is the FHIR Bulk Data API documentation, which is explicitly scoped to USCDI/(g)(10). For a radiation oncology system like ARIA — where the majority of clinically significant data (treatment plans, fraction logs, physics data, DICOM images) lives outside the USCDI scope — using the FHIR API as a (b)(10) export would leave the vast majority of the designated record set unexported.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}
